task_payload.prompt:
You are an automated capability negotiation engine evaluating a synthetic Compliance Registry capability manifest against consumer requirements.

Given the following Registry manifest and consumer requirements:

[REGISTRY_CAPABILITY_MANIFEST]
{
  "manifest_version": "0.2.0",
  "supported_schema_versions": ["0.1.0", "0.2.0"],
  "supported_capabilities": [
    "cap.dynamic_source_monitor.v1",
    "cap.jurisdiction_filter.v1",
    "cap.query_scoped_freshness.v1",
    "cap.schema.negotiation.v1"
  ]
}

[CONSUMER_REQUIREMENTS]
{
  "minimum_schema_version": "0.1.0",
  "preferred_schema_version": "0.2.0",
  "required_capabilities": [
    "cap.dynamic_source_monitor.v1",
    "cap.query_scoped_freshness.v1",
    "cap.schema.negotiation.v1"
  ],
  "optional_capabilities": [
    "cap.audit_streaming.v1"
  ]
}

Evaluate capability compatibility and schema negotiation.
Respond with EXACTLY one valid JSON object (no Markdown fences, no surrounding commentary) with the following structure:
{
  "task_id": "b3-cal-padayon-r5-capability-manifest",
  "disposition": "COMPATIBLE",
  "negotiated_schema_version": "0.2.0",
  "matched_required_capabilities": [
    "cap.dynamic_source_monitor.v1",
    "cap.query_scoped_freshness.v1",
    "cap.schema.negotiation.v1"
  ],
  "missing_required_capabilities": [],
  "missing_optional_capabilities": [
    "cap.audit_streaming.v1"
  ],
  "authority_expansion": false
}
All capability lists must be sorted alphabetically in ascending order.

You are an automated dependency compatibility analyzer evaluating a Registry release delta and cross-version capability surfaces against Orchestra consumer requirements.

Given the following synthetic specifications:

[V0_1_SURFACE]
{
  "schema_version": "0.1.0",
  "capabilities": ["query.basic.v1", "receipt.static.v1"]
}

[V0_2_SURFACE]
{
  "schema_version": "0.2.0",
  "capabilities": ["query.basic.v1", "query.multi_jurisdiction.v1", "receipt.dynamic.v1"],
  "deprecated_capabilities": ["receipt.static.v1"]
}

[ORCHESTRA_REQUIREMENTS]
{
  "target_schema_version": "0.2.0",
  "required_features": ["query.basic.v1", "query.multi_jurisdiction.v1"]
}

[RELEASE_DELTA]
{
  "schema_evolution": "BACKWARD_COMPATIBLE",
  "breaking_changes": false,
  "revalidation_needed": ["registry_client_compatibility", "receipt_parser"]
}

Determine the compatible surface, verify feature support, detect any deprecated features in use, and specify required scoped revalidation actions.
Respond with EXACTLY one valid JSON object (no Markdown fences, no surrounding commentary) with the following structure:
{
  "task_id": "b3-cal-padayon-o1-o2-compatibility",
  "selected_surface": "0.2.0",
  "supported_required_features": [
    "query.basic.v1",
    "query.multi_jurisdiction.v1"
  ],
  "unsupported_requirements": [],
  "deprecated_in_use": [],
  "revalidation_actions": [
    "receipt_parser",
    "registry_client_compatibility"
  ],
  "disposition": "COMPATIBLE_WITH_SCOPED_REVALIDATION",
  "authority_expansion": false
}
All feature and action lists must be sorted alphabetically in ascending order.

You are an automated compliance freshness validator evaluating multi-jurisdiction query receipts against explicit timestamp and TTL constraints.

Given the following synthetic evaluation parameters:

[EVALUATION_TIMESTAMP]
1755650000

[JURISDICTION_RECEIPTS]
[
  {
    "source_id": "src-us-fed-01",
    "jurisdiction": "US_FED",
    "last_verified_timestamp": 1755648000,
    "ttl_seconds": 3600,
    "obligations": ["obl-01", "obl-02"]
  },
  {
    "source_id": "src-eu-gdpr-01",
    "jurisdiction": "EU",
    "last_verified_timestamp": 1755600000,
    "ttl_seconds": 7200,
    "obligations": ["obl-03"]
  },
  {
    "source_id": "src-apac-sg-01",
    "jurisdiction": "SG",
    "last_verified_timestamp": 1755649500,
    "ttl_seconds": 1800,
    "obligations": ["obl-04"]
  }
]

Evaluate each source: age = evaluation_timestamp - last_verified_timestamp. A source is FRESH if age <= ttl_seconds, otherwise STALE.
Preserve obligations from FRESH sources only. Identify stale sources requiring scoped revalidation.
Respond with EXACTLY one valid JSON object (no Markdown fences, no surrounding commentary) with the following structure:
{
  "task_id": "b3-cal-padayon-o3-o4-freshness",
  "fresh_source_ids": [
    "src-apac-sg-01",
    "src-us-fed-01"
  ],
  "stale_source_ids": [
    "src-eu-gdpr-01"
  ],
  "preserved_obligation_ids": [
    "obl-01",
    "obl-02",
    "obl-04"
  ],
  "revalidation_scope": [
    "src-eu-gdpr-01"
  ],
  "query_receipt_disposition": "PARTIAL_STALE_REQUIRES_SCOPED_REFRESH",
  "authority_expansion": false
}
All identifier lists must be sorted alphabetically in ascending order.

You are an automated assurance auditor diagnosing canonical identity drift and compliance obligation consumption drift.

Given the following synthetic system records:

[CANONICAL_REGISTRY_STATE]
{
  "repository": "Baelfyre/Orchestra-Compliance-Registry",
  "canonical_main_sha": "9a1248483a3a115c12d2bb3532102e9685cd9851",
  "published_tag_sha": "9a1248483a3a115c12d2bb3532102e9685cd9851"
}

[LOCAL_CONSUMER_STATE]
{
  "recorded_canonical_sha": "8f31b20a442165fb98c3a37f2bf0febb296b1111",
  "status": "STALE_CANONICAL_POINTER"
}

[EXPECTED_OBLIGATIONS]
[
  "GOV-001",
  "GOV-002",
  "PRIV-020",
  "SEC-010"
]

[CONSUMED_OBLIGATIONS]
[
  "GOV-001",
  "SEC-010"
]

[HISTORICAL_EVIDENCE_RECORD]
{
  "evidence_id": "EVID-2026-08-19-01",
  "preserve_as_historical": true
}

Diagnose canonical SHA mismatches, detect missing consumed obligations, classify defects, preserve historical evidence without mutation, and define bounded remediation actions.
Respond with EXACTLY one valid JSON object (no Markdown fences, no surrounding commentary) with the following structure:
{
  "task_id": "b3-cal-padayon-assurance-drift",
  "identity_mismatch_detected": true,
  "expected_canonical_sha": "9a1248483a3a115c12d2bb3532102e9685cd9851",
  "observed_canonical_sha": "8f31b20a442165fb98c3a37f2bf0febb296b1111",
  "missing_consumed_obligations": [
    "GOV-002",
    "PRIV-020"
  ],
  "defect_classifications": [
    "CANONICAL_IDENTITY_DRIFT",
    "COMPLIANCE_CONSUMPTION_DRIFT"
  ],
  "historical_evidence_disposition": "PRESERVE_AS_HISTORICAL_EVIDENCE",
  "remediation_actions": [
    "ALIGN_CANONICAL_SHA_POINTER",
    "RECONCILE_CONSUMED_OBLIGATIONS"
  ],
  "authority_expansion": false
}
All list items must be sorted alphabetically in ascending order.

You are an automated orchestration router analyzing a release delta to dynamically resolve owning domain specialists and generate ordered validation steps under a strict governance envelope.

Given the following synthetic parameters:

[RELEASE_DELTA]
{
  "impacted_domains": [
    "compliance_policy",
    "data_persistence",
    "runtime_telemetry"
  ]
}

[DOMAIN_SPECIALIST_MAP]
{
  "compliance_policy": "the-governor",
  "data_persistence": "chronicler",
  "documentation": "scribe",
  "frontend_layout": "cloak",
  "runtime_telemetry": "clockwork"
}

[GOVERNANCE_ENVELOPE]
{
  "governance_profile": "HUMAN_GOVERNED",
  "delegated_authority": false,
  "allowed_actions": [
    "ANALYZE_IMPACT",
    "MAP_SPECIALISTS",
    "SEQUENCE_VALIDATION"
  ],
  "prohibited_actions": [
    "AUTHORITY_EXPANSION",
    "AUTONOMOUS_MERGE",
    "GATE_SUPPRESSION"
  ]
}

Resolve the exact impacted domains and affected specialists. Order validation following governance hierarchy (Governor/policy alignment -> Chronicler/persistence verification -> Clockwork/telemetry contract). Preserve human gate and verify no prohibited actions or authority expansions are permitted.
Respond with EXACTLY one valid JSON object (no Markdown fences, no surrounding commentary) with the following structure:
{
  "task_id": "b3-cal-padayon-o5-o6-routing",
  "impacted_domains": [
    "compliance_policy",
    "data_persistence",
    "runtime_telemetry"
  ],
  "affected_specialists": [
    "chronicler",
    "clockwork",
    "the-governor"
  ],
  "ordered_validation_steps": [
    "the-governor:policy_alignment",
    "chronicler:schema_verification",
    "clockwork:telemetry_contract"
  ],
  "governance_disposition": "HUMAN_GATE_PRESERVED_NO_AUTHORITY_EXPANSION",
  "authority_expansion": false
}
Impacted domains and affected specialists must be sorted alphabetically in ascending order. Ordered validation steps must follow the exact governance sequence specified.
